question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Aug 26, 2026 Q2 FY27 call, CFO Kress said gross margin should bottom at 71-72% in Q4 FY27 because of memory costs, then recover to 72-73% in FY28. The Q3 guide was 74.0% +/-50bp, with GAAP equal to non-GAAP. The formal Q4 guide midpoint therefore most likely lands near 71.5%. Downside risk: memory costs keep rising, or GAAP-only charges. Upside risk: price increases arrive early. Polymarket only prices Q3 actual non-GAAP margin (73-75% at 0.83, thin volume), which is a near-miss contract, so it is evidence only; it implies Q3 is tracking the 74% guide. No market found on the Q4 guide itself.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (Aug 26, 2026 PR): revenue $96.2B; GAAP and non-GAAP GM both 75.0%. Q3 guide: GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp; revenue $108B +/-2% (NVIDIA PR; Investing.com).
- Aug 26, 2026 call (Fool, Oct 10, 2026; CNBC/gamesreviews headlines): CFO Kress said GM 'should bottom out at 71% to 72% in the fiscal fourth quarter', mainly because of memory prices; FY28 GM to settle at 72-73% once price increases already in place take effect.
- Kress quote (r40.io): memory price increases 'exceeded our prior expectations and are headed even higher into next year'.
- Bloomberg-compiled consensus (via search snippet): Q4 FY27 GM below 72%.
- GAAP vs non-GAAP GM: identical in the last two quarters; historically GAAP ran 0.1-0.3pt below non-GAAP.
- Status quo: the formal Q4 guide matches the stated 71-72% trough, so the midpoint is near 71.5.
- Precedent: in FY25, management said 'low 70s' during the Blackwell ramp and then guided Q4 FY25 GAAP at about 70.5-71%.
- Upside drivers: price increases implemented early; memory relief; product mix. Downside drivers: further memory spikes; GAAP-only charges (inventory, acquisition amortization).
- Resolves off the GAAP GM midpoint in the 'Outlook' section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected Nov 17, 2026), rounded to 0.1%; not non-GAAP and not call commentary.
- Event window: single release on Nov 17, 2026; as of Oct 29, 2026 the release has not happened.
- Searched without finding: any intra-quarter update (Oct 2026) to the Q4 margin trajectory, and any prediction market on the Q4 guide itself (Polymarket only covers Q3 actual non-GAAP GM).

NVIDIA's X% ±50bp guide format and recent GAAP=non-GAAP guides point to a 71.5% midpoint, with 71.0 and 72.0 plausible alternatives. Downside: memory costs rising further, or GAAP printing slightly below non-GAAP. Upside: price increases arriving early, or the earlier statement having been conservative. No market prices the Q4 guide; Polymarket's thin Q3 non-GAAP brackets (0.83 on 73-75%) only suggest Q3 is on track.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs cite the same anchor: the CFO's 71-72% Q4 trough statement, with Q3 guided at 74.0% ±50bp and GAAP equal to non-GAAP. They differ only in tail width, mostly the upper tail (90th percentile 72.1-72.4). That is a judgment call: no run found an intra-quarter update. The >15% server price increases apply to systems shipping early next year, so they mostly fall after this quarter, and memory costs are rising. Those offset, so I keep a near-symmetric tail at 72.2. The GAAP/non-GAAP gap is a factual question I cannot settle here (zero in the last two quarters, 0.1-0.5pt historically), so it stays as a small downside skew. I carry forward the runs' reference class and a width of ~1.4. I retrieved nothing new on this run.

disagreements.verdict: The price increases mostly land after Q4 and memory costs keep rising, so they offset; I took 72.2
